newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases down from high prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases down from high prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened down 90 basis points at 24.60 percent on Thursday, below to what traders said was an unrepresentatively high prior close.
Nonetheless, dealers said secondary rates could come under renewed upside pressure from recent central bank participation and speculation by big players holding hefty liquidity positions.
"Yesterday's short-term (central bank participation) rates are forcing rates up. They were very high yesterday," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico participated in the secondary market on Wednesday by offering 10 repurchase agreements totalling 6.423 billion pesos, at rates of 23.45-26.11 percent.
Traders said draining liquidity through repurchase agreements was a marked change from offering auctions, which had been the central bank's method of participating since the beginning of the year.

"It looks like the rise in (primary) rates (on Tuesday) was insufficient and firmly anchored, so then the central bank offered paper, fixed secondary rates, and so speculators are taking advantage of those rates," the trader added.
Traders said most market liquidity was concentrated in few hands, a situation that lent itself to secondary rates gaining on speculation.
Early firmness on the peso due to capital inflow into the secondary market was a sign that rates were high, traders added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were unchanged at 7.8740/7.8880 per dollar in early trade.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile down 45 basis points at 26.05 percent.
Liquidity of 10.108 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
